subject: TitanEdge — market parity & EU territory exclusivity request (escalation)
messages:
From: Lena Kline <lena.kline@titanedge.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@titanedge.com
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partnership proposal — EU commercial terms

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. TitanEdge is excited about embedding Redwood across our EU product line. At a high level our procurement team needs two commercial items cleared before we can proceed to SOW: a market-parity (MFN) clause covering comparable tier pricing for 24 months, and a limited territorial exclusivity for EU public-sector tenders for 18 months.

We’re prepared to agree to a multi-year commitment and are asking for a 40% list discount on standard per-token pricing if those clauses are included. I’ve attached the current SOW draft and the procurement checklist for your reference.

Can your team advise whether these terms are possible and what approvals are needed? We’d like to finalize commercials by end of next week to hit a June launch.

Best,
Lena Kline
VP Partnerships, TitanEdge
attachments: TitanEdge_SOW_v3.pdf, procurement-checklist.pdf

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc:
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Partnership proposal — EU commercial terms (need deal desk + exec review)

Team — forwarding Lena’s note. Key asks: 24-month MFN, 18-month EU public-sector exclusivity, 40% off list. They’re proposing a multi-year commit.

Why I’m escalating: 1) MFN duration and breadth are outside standard policy; 2) exclusivity for public-sector in EU creates go-to-market restrictions that could block future partners; 3) discount depth materially impacts unit economics at the expected volume.

Please advise: what would Deal Desk recommend (narrow MFN, limited carve-outs, shorter duration?), and what level of executive signoff is required?

I’ve tentatively suggested we hold off on legal redlines until we have a commercial signal.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0142

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partnership proposal — EU commercial terms (Deal Desk intake)

Grace — thanks for the flag. Quick Deal Desk read below (see attached redline + pricing scenarios).

Summary of risk:
- MFN (24m) covering "comparable tier pricing" without strict definitions exposes us to downstream price resets across segments.
- Territorial exclusivity for public-sector tenders (18m) could preclude channel-led opportunities and conflicts with reseller agreements we already have in several EU markets.
- 40% off list at forecasted volume drives blended unit below our target LTV/CAC thresholds unless we secure a minimum committed usage (we should ask for a ARR/commitment floor).

Recommendation:
1) Accept a *narrow* MFN: 12 months, limited to the exact SKU set and billing currency, with explicit carve-outs for partner reseller agreements and promotional discounts.
2) Replace exclusivity with a right-of-first-refusal for public-sector procurements for 12 months (adds time for GTM coordination without blocking existing channel motions).
3) Offer 30% discount contingent on a 24-month minimum committed spend (include ramp schedule).

Attachments: pricing-sheet.xlsx, redwood_mfn_draft.docx (contains suggested MFN language and carve-outs).

If Sales wants to keep exclusivity we should escalate to VP Revenue for one-time exception and require a commercial collar (commitment + pricing floors).

- Jonas
Deal Desk Manager

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partnership proposal — EU commercial terms (quick take from Revenue)

Appreciate the summary, Jonas. My quick take: we should avoid a broad MFN longer than 12 months. 24 months is a hard no without a very significant commitment and board-level approval — it ties our hands across multiple accounts.

On exclusivity: public-sector exclusives are sticky. If we consider any concession there, it must be narrowly scoped (specific procurement IDs or defined program lines) and paired with strong co-selling commitments and a non-circumvention clause.

Commercial counter I’d support: 30% off list, 12-month narrow MFN with partner carve-outs, 12-month right-of-first-refusal for EU public tenders, and a minimum committed spend of $3.2M ARR over 24 months. If they want exclusivity instead of ROFR, escalate to Kate (VP Revenue) and Finance for final signoff.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Lena Kline <lena.kline@titanedge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 May 2029 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership proposal — EU commercial terms

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask and for the SOW. We reviewed internally and have a commercial counterproposal we can put in writing: 30% off list, a targeted 12-month MFN that applies only to the agreed SKU list and billing currency with partner carve-outs, and a 12-month right-of-first-refusal on EU public-sector tenders (we’d need a short list of programs to scope). We’d also need a 24-month minimum committed spend (we’re proposing $3.2M ARR) with a ramp schedule.

Per the internal guidance from Deal Desk and Revenue, we can consider exclusivity only as a last resort with executive approval and a commercial collar; that will need Kate’s signoff and Finance review. I’ve attached the proposed MFN wording and a pricing scenario for transparency.

If that’s in line with TitanEdge’s expectations, we can circulate a redline and get Legal involved. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow to go through the details.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_mfn_draft.docx, pricing-sheet.xlsx
